rationale: Oakland's 2023 vacant-property-tax finding for this parcel was upheld on judicial review in 2026; the court found the owner's storage claim did not establish qualifying use. A 2024 redevelopment application does not prove construction or occupancy. Current vacancy and its start date remain unverified.
duration_note: City vacancy determination applies to tax year 2023; no start date or continuous duration is established.

evidence.source_name: DecisionDepot case record, Center 5th Street LLC v. City of Oakland, 25CV148214
evidence.supports: The court record concerns 375 Center Street and describes notices issued 2024-03-22 and 2024-05-03 for the 2023 vacant-property-tax assessment, the 2024-07-02 administrative hearing, and denial of the owner's writ petition on 2026-08-07. City evidence included blight/disrepair and no associated business license; the owner's storage claim did not establish qualifying use or the required 40% occupied storage area. The court record says the City acknowledged a redevelopment planning permit could support an exemption in 2024 and later if in place.
evidence.limitation: Published case-record reproduction, not the court docket-hosted original; confirms a 2023 assessment only, not continuous or present-day vacancy. It also records a possible later-year redevelopment exemption without establishing whether one was granted.

evidence.supports: The court had received no objections to the proposed judgment and would enter it; the compliance hearing was vacated.
evidence.limitation: Published case-record reproduction, not the court portal's original; procedural outcome only, no evidence of present-day occupancy.
